title: NRG-LU001: no survival benefit from adding metformin to chemoradiation

Q01.answer: Test metformin added to chemoradiation in stage III NSCLC. Prespecified primary one-year progression-free survival. Cancer control and survival. Not a trial of diabetes management.

Q02.answer: Adults with unresectable stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC without diabetes. Zubrod performance status 0–1; 79 institutions in US, Canada and Israel. 170 enrolled, three ineligible excluded; 86 metformin and 81 control analyzed. The eligible ITT population is 167.

Q03.answer: Oral metformin tablets. Escalated over two weeks to 2000 mg/day during chemoradiation and consolidation chemotherapy. Both groups received 60 Gy radiation, weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel and two consolidation cycles. Median follow-up among survivors 27.7 months. This regimen predates routine consolidation immunotherapy.

Q04.answer: Same chemoradiation without metformin. Central 1:1 assignment stratified by performance, histology and stage. Zelen permuted-block scheme. Open-label; central imaging reviewer masked to assignment. Concurrent randomized comparison. Masked imaging review reduces but does not eliminate open-label limitations.

Q05.answer: Primary PFS; secondary overall survival, recurrence and toxicity. RECIST 1.1 progression or death; CTCAE 4.03 toxicity. One-year primary estimate, longer time-to-event follow-up. Clinical cancer endpoints. Design targeted 15-point one-year PFS improvement, 50% to 65%; not a universal MCID. Do not equate response biomarkers with these outcomes.

Q06.answer: One-year PFS 51.3% metformin versus 60.4% control; OS 80.8% versus 80.2%. Eligible population 86 versus 81; survival percentages are Kaplan-Meier estimates, not simple event fractions. PFS HR 1.15, CI 0.77–1.73; OS HR 1.03, CI 0.64–1.68. Estimated PFS difference −9.1 percentage points, calculated from rounded reported rates. Primary reported P=.24; blinded imaging sensitivity HR 1.09, CI 0.69–1.73. No survival benefit demonstrated; uncertainty does not establish equivalence.

Q07.answer: Radiation received by 74/86 versus 75/81. Time-to-event censoring; not all randomized patients received protocol therapy. 52 patients, 63.4% of the reported adherence denominator, completed the metformin course; only 39% maintained full dose without modification. Three eligibility exclusions after randomization. Eligible ITT for efficacy, treated safety population. Individual patient. Treatment completion and outcome availability must remain distinct.

Q08.answer: CTCAE assessment at follow-up; protocol-related toxicity tabulated. 79 metformin and 75 control. At least one grade 3+ event: 52/79 versus 51/75; grade 5 events one versus four, none deemed potentially treatment-related. Metformin adverse effects were the most common reason for its discontinuation. During treatment and scheduled follow-up. Comparable severe-event rates do not mean no gastrointestinal burden.

Q09.answer: Open-label, phase II sample and incomplete full-dose exposure; masked imaging a strength. Randomization limits confounding; background care and adherence affect interpretation. Full separately linked protocol and supplementary tables not acquired in this packet. Several secondary comparisons; avoid selecting isolated trends. Wide efficacy intervals; trial designed for a large improvement. Abstract age IQR differs slightly from full-cohort table; no harmonization needed for guide conclusions. No validated subgroup rescue of the null result.

Q10.answer: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without diabetes. 2000 mg/day with specified carboplatin/paclitaxel regimen. Does not support adding metformin to improve survival. Not all lung cancer stages, molecular therapies or modern immunotherapy combinations were tested. Do not generalize a regimen-specific null to diabetes treatment.

Q11.answer: NRG-LU001 independent trial. ALMERA is a separate Canadian trial with different chemotherapy and duration. No duplicate cohort identified between these named trials. Current guide sources, not exhaustive NSCLC review. Both should be presented without pooling incompatible primary endpoints.

Q12.answer: Heath Skinner, Chen Hu, Theodoros Tsakiridis and colleagues. NRG Oncology multicenter network. NCI grants; NRG/NCI involved in design, conduct, analysis and publication. Donated-product source not established in inspected text. Several investigators disclosed grants, consulting and other industry relationships. Disclosures are documented, not used as a substitute for appraisal.

Q13.answer: Published JAMA Oncology 2021, DOI 10.1001/jamaoncol.2021.2318. Full article including tables acquired. Supplement 1 protocol and Supplement 2 not separately recovered. NCT02186847 identified in report; separate registry not audited here. No correction/retraction identified in retrieved records. November 3–4, 2026. Main-report assessment supports the bounded null conclusion.

Q14.answer: Adding metformin to chemoradiation. No demonstrated PFS or OS benefit. Authors' clinical conclusion agrees with observed comparisons; do not convert mechanistic rationale into efficacy. Retain dose-completion limitations.

Q15.answer: Routine anticancer addition is not supported by this trial. Other modern regimens remain separate questions. Direct randomized evidence in those regimens would be necessary. Do not infer cancer benefit from glucose lowering.

appraisal: Randomized phase II evidence did not show improved progression-free or overall survival. Open-label treatment, incomplete dosing and broad confidence intervals limit precision, while blinded imaging review supports the robustness of the null comparison.
